summary: [TechDept] [EP:dev] PaymentInvoiceService: tolerate null ambient lang when generating invoices (TypeError hardening)

ai.s: Hardens invoice generation so a null ambient language no longer throws a TypeError that could return a 500 after a payment has already succeeded.
ai.pr: PaymentInvoiceService defaulted language from a static that can be null into a typed string property, so in a narrow corner invoice generation could crash after booking side effects.
ai.wy: Tech debt agreed in the PR #4578 review: the hazard is real though rare, and would give clients a 500 for a recorded success.
ai.oc: Invoice generation is to tolerate a null language across the four no-language call sites, closing the TypeError path.

summary: [Tech debt] - Chosen [Anchor option] is not updated after element [Anchor] rename

ai.s: Keeps the chosen anchor option on linked buttons and links in sync when the anchor element is renamed in the site builder.
ai.pr: After an anchor element was renamed, buttons and links pointing to it kept showing the old anchor option.
ai.wy: Frontend tech debt; stale anchor links break on-page navigation that organisers have set up.
ai.oc: Renaming an anchor is to update the anchor option selected on linked clickable elements.

summary: Community-as-home-page redirect drops query params and URL fragment

ai.s: Makes the community-as-home-page redirect keep query parameters, the URL fragment and the locale, so links such as /#signIn still work.
ai.pr: With the community page set as home, the root rendered 200 then hard-navigated to a bare /community, dropping the query string, fragment and Redux store, and omitting the locale.
ai.wy: Frontend routing tech debt: deep links like the sign-in modal were silently broken on community-as-home sites.
ai.oc: The redirect target is to carry query, fragment and locale through, avoiding the lossy client-side hop.

summary: Migrate Statistic Events from WebSocket to HTTP ingest gateway

ai.s: Moves browser statistic events off the shared WebSocket to the data science team's HTTP ingest gateway, which validates and forwards them to S3 and ClickHouse.
ai.pr: Analytics went browser → WebSocket → our backend → DS, some events never arrived, and the message shape was awkward to consume.
ai.wy: The data science team is replacing the path, taking our backend out of the analytics flow.
ai.oc: The three analytics WS actions (statistics, online dwell, notification clicks) are to post to the ingest gateway; chat, presence and push stay on WebSocket.

summary: Enforce per-event access scope for configured admins (deny-by-default in AccessControl)

ai.s: Admins restricted on one event stay restricted on every event they have not been explicitly granted, instead of falling back to the default access template.
ai.pr: An admin set to view-only or no access on one event resolved against the tenant's permissive DEFAULT SETTINGS on other events, silently bypassing the restriction.
ai.wy: Organisers expect per-event restrictions to hold; the bypass is a security and trust issue.
ai.oc: A new resolution order is defined: explicit row wins, any configured admin is denied elsewhere, and only never-configured admins use DEFAULT SETTINGS.

summary: Post Code Field Validation for Registration Forms

ai.s: Adds validation for the post code field on registration forms (details are in a linked Confluence page only).
ai.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumably registration forms accepted post codes without format validation.
ai.wy: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
ai.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to validate post codes entered in registration forms.

summary: All 404s return HTTP 200 — soft-404 caused by the next-i18n-router rewrite

ai.s: Makes non-existent pages return a real HTTP 404 instead of 200, fixing soft-404s caused by the next-i18n-router rewrite.
ai.pr: The locale-rewriting middleware dropped the 404 status, so every missing URL on every tenant site returned 200 OK with 404 content.
ai.wy: SEO and monitoring: junk paths were indexable and uptime checks could not tell broken routes from healthy ones.
ai.oc: The status loss is to be pinned down in the rewrite path and fixed so notFound() yields a 404 across the app, including site-builder slugs.

summary: Utils::addToQueue reports its own SQS failure through itself — exponential retry loop that OOMs the process

ai.s: Stops Utils::addToQueue reporting its own SQS failures through itself, which created a growing retry loop that ran the process out of memory.
ai.pr: When the SQS publish failed, the catch block called sendException, which re-entered addToQueue via the Discord queue, looping with payloads growing about sixfold per turn.
ai.wy: A generic reliability defect found during testing of EP-53978; any SQS outage or credential issue could crash processes.
ai.oc: The failure path is to be decoupled from the queue it reports on, so an SQS failure is logged once rather than looping to OOM.

summary: Re-check which interaction events reach ClickHouse for an opted-out actor, and decide per action

ai.s: Audits which interaction events still reach ClickHouse for users who opted out of networking, and decides per action whether to suppress them.
ai.pr: Consent was checked nowhere on the analytics write path, so opted-out users could still be identified to others through analytics; EP-53978 fixed only favourites.
ai.wy: Privacy and GDPR: decide the remaining ~40 action codes deliberately rather than defect by defect.
ai.oc: A per-action table over AnalyticsActionEnum is to record emit channel, whether it identifies the actor and the decision to keep or suppress.

summary: [TechDept] [adminUI] Sentry: tag events with tenant and user identity

ai.s: Tags adminUI Sentry events with tenant, event and user identity so errors can be found by customer.
ai.pr: No Sentry event from adminUI carried tenant or user identity; setUser and setTag had zero uses across all 162 repos.
ai.wy: Observability: support and engineering need to search errors by customer.
ai.oc: After auth, setUser plus ep.tenant and ep.event_id tags are to be set and cleared on logout, using indexed tags rather than contexts.

summary: [portalUI] Sentry: tag events with tenant and user identity

ai.s: Tags portalUI Sentry events with tenant, event and user identity so errors can be found by customer.
ai.pr: No Sentry event from portalUI carried any tenant or user identity, so errors could not be traced to a customer.
ai.wy: Observability, aligned with the adminUI sibling ticket so one search works across both projects.
ai.oc: After auth, setUser plus ep.tenant and ep.event_id tags are to be set and cleared on logout, using the same tag names as adminUI.

summary: [TechDept] [adminUI] Sentry: upload source maps so production stack traces are readable

ai.s: Uploads adminUI source maps to Sentry so production stack traces show real functions and lines instead of minified bundle positions.
ai.pr: adminUI built with sourcemap: false and no Sentry Vite plugin, so production traces pointed at minified code.
ai.wy: Observability: readable traces are needed to diagnose production errors.
ai.oc: Hidden source maps are to be generated, uploaded via @sentry/vite-plugin with a secured CI token, deleted locally, and matched to the runtime release.

summary: [portalUI] Sentry: confirm source map upload is not silently skipped in CI

ai.s: Confirms portalUI source map uploads to Sentry actually run in CI rather than being silently skipped when the auth token is missing.
ai.pr: portalUI's Sentry config used dryRun when SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN was absent, so uploads could silently no-op and nobody would know.
ai.wy: Observability: silently minified traces are only discovered when someone needs them.
ai.oc: The token is to be checked or added as a secured pipeline variable, with an option to fail the production build when it is missing.

summary: [portalUI] Sentry: Report a problem action that flushes the replay buffer

ai.s: Adds a portalUI "Report a problem" action that flushes the Sentry replay buffer and sends users to intake with the feedback event id.
ai.pr: Replays only uploaded on exceptions, so bugs that throw nothing, such as wrong totals or dead buttons, had no evidence.
ai.wy: Turns prose bug reports into reports with the actual session, breadcrumbs and network calls attached.
ai.oc: The action is to flush replay, call captureFeedback and pass the event id to intake, using the same URL parameter as adminUI and no SDK upgrade.

summary: [TechDept] [adminUI] Sentry: Report a problem action that flushes the replay buffer

ai.s: Adds an adminUI "Report a problem" action that flushes the Sentry replay buffer and sends users to intake with the feedback event id.
ai.pr: Replays only uploaded on exceptions and just 5% of sessions were recorded, so non-throwing bugs arrived as unreproducible prose.
ai.wy: Gives support the real session evidence for reported problems and makes use of the replay buffer already kept.
ai.oc: The action is to await replay flush, call captureFeedback and pass the event id to intake on the current @sentry/react v10 SDK.

summary: [adminUI] Sentry: Report a problem action that flushes the replay buffer

ai.s: Adds an adminUI "Report a problem" action that flushes the Sentry replay buffer and sends users to intake with the feedback event id (duplicate of the TechDept ticket).
ai.pr: Replays only uploaded on exceptions and just 5% of sessions were recorded, so non-throwing bugs arrived as unreproducible prose.
ai.wy: Gives support the real session evidence for reported problems and makes use of the replay buffer already kept.
ai.oc: The action is to await replay flush, call captureFeedback and pass the event id to intake on the current @sentry/react v10 SDK.

summary: Meeting report extension. Subject and Message

ai.s: Extends the meetings report with Subject and Message columns (detail is in a linked Confluence page only).
ai.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumably the meetings report lacked the meeting subject and message.
ai.wy: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title.
ai.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; presumed to add Subject and Message columns to the meetings report.

summary: Decide the source of truth for favourite counters: keep ClickHouse-only (accept the gap) or emit favourites server-side

ai.s: Decides the source of truth for profile favourite counters: keep ClickHouse and accept the gap, or emit favourites server-side.
ai.pr: Favourite counters summed a ClickHouse public count and a Postgres private count, so API-created favourites were missed and opted-out clicks double-counted.
ai.wy: Three parked defects (EP-55702, EP-55697, EP-55707) share this root cause and cannot be fixed until the decision is made.
ai.oc: A decision ticket lays out the measured under- and over-counts and why moving to Postgres alone is not possible.

summary: Replace ParamPOS with Iyzico

ai.s: Adds Iyzico as a native payment gateway, including instalments, to replace ParamPOS for organisers taking Turkish card payments.
ai.pr: ParamPOS could no longer process transactions, leaving events with Turkish card payments without a working gateway.
ai.wy: Keep registration revenue flowing for organisers who rely on Turkish card payments.
ai.oc: An Iyzico driver, Event Setup panel, validators and webhook handling are specified, recording payments like Stripe and PayPal with clear error states.

summary: Unique Link Support in Marketing Campaigns

ai.s: Organisers can import an external badge URL per participant and insert it into campaign emails as an "External Badge Link" variable.
ai.pr: The external_badge_url field could only be filled by the Visit G2/GES integration and could not be used in marketing campaigns.
ai.wy: Requested by CloserStill to send each participant a unique badge link from campaigns.
ai.oc: Participant CSV import is to set external_badge_url and the Email Builder is to offer an External Badge Link variable resolved per recipient.
